name: Kim Kardashian
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2015); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Kim Kardashian has parlayed reality TV stardom into a ten-figure fortune, the vast majority of which comes from her stake in Skims, her shapewear business.
Skims is worth $5 billion after a 2025 funding round. The company's investors include billionaires Stephen Mandel, Daniel Sundheim and Josh Kushner, who is Ivanka Trump's brother-in-law.
Skims began as an online, direct-to-consumer brand, but has grown to 20 stores in the U.S. and Mexico with plans to become a mainly brick-and-mortar business in the coming years.
Kardashian sold 20% of her KKW Beauty to French beauty giant Coty in 2021, but later shut down the business and launched SKKN By Kim. Coty divested its stake to Skims in March 2025.
Kardashian divorced musician Kanye West in 2022. They share custody of their four children, and Kardashian reportedly paid $23 million to keep their Axel Vervoordt-designed Hidden Hills mansion.
forbes_facts: Kardashian is an advocate for criminal justice reform, gun safety and cancer causes.
Kadashian has some of the most-followed social media pages in the world: 72 million on X and 354 million on Instagram.

name: Azad Moopen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2017); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Physician Azad Moopen started Aster DM Healthcare with one clinic in Dubai in 1987.
Today his healthcare empire has a network of 54 hospitals, including 15 in the Middle East and 39 in India.
Moopen listed the Duabi-based company on the Indian bourses in 2018.
forbes_facts: His U.S.-educated daughter Alisha overseas strategy.

name: Pu Zhongjie
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2020-2023); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2022)
forbes_bio: Pu Zhongjie chairs Shenzhen-listed company Lepu Medical Technology (Beijing).
Lepu Medical,  founded in 1999, produces medical equipment and devices such as coronary stents, mechanical heart valves and spinal implants.
The company has subsidiaries in Netherland, Turkey and India and has built distribution channels in over 80 countries.

name: José Coppel Luken
forbes_bio: José Coppel and his four brothers own Grupo Coppel, a Mexican conglomerate with over 1,700 department stores.
Their father and grandfather founded the first shop in 1941 selling radios and watches. Today, the stores sell everything from clothing to electronics.
The stores are known for providing credit to customers, allowing them to finance their purchases over multiple payments.
The group expanded into the banking sector with BanCoppel in 2007.
forbes_facts: The brothers also have two sisters who don't have active roles in the business.

name: Yoshiaki Yoshida
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Yoshiaki Yoshida is the founder of Japanese beauty brand DHC. He started the company in 1972 to provide translation services.
In 1980, he started the cosmetics business using organic olives. In 1983, he got into the mail order segment. It also sells nutritional supplements and health foods.
The privately held company sells both through retail stores and online.
In 2023, Yoshida sold his company to Japanese leasing giant Orix, which valued it at ¥300 billion.
forbes_facts: DHC stands for Daigaku Honyaku Center.
Yoshida is a supporter of conservative political causes and has his own TV production company providing online and broadcast content.
DHC sources its olive oil from organic olive groves in Spain.

name: Carlos Sanchez
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Carlos Sanchez owns and runs privately-held generic drug firm EMS S.A., which was founded by his late father.
EMS S.A. sells prescription, generic, branded generic and over-the-counter products.
In recent years, the company has benefited from adding drugs including generic versions of Viagra and Lipitor to its sales arsenal.
EMS was founded by Sanchez' father, Emiliano, in 1950 as a small pharmacy. Sanchez inherited EMS at age 26 when his father died.
Sanchez owns 75% of EMS; the rest is owned by the sons of his sister, who passed away in 2009.
forbes_facts: Sanchez reportedly bid $85 million for Edvard Munch painting The Scream at a Sotheby's auction but was outbid by billionaire Leon Black at $119.9 million.

name: Thomas von Koch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Thomas von Koch joined publicly traded Swedish investment company EQT AB at its founding in 1994.
He ran EQT as CEO and managing partner from 2014 to 2019.
Von Koch owns 4% of EQT, which has roughly $62 billion (52 billion Euro) in assets under management.
EQT primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
EQT's portfolio include Nestl? Skin Health and open-source software company SUSE, which EQT acquired in 2019 for $2.5 billion.
forbes_facts: Thomas von Koch lives with his family in Hong Kong.

name: Wang Wenyin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2023); Hurun China (2013-2023); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Wang Wenyin is the founder of copper and cable conglomerate Amer.
Headquartered in Shenzhen, Amer has 30,000 employees globally with offices in Asia, the U.S. and Europe.
Wang's roots to Shenzhen trace back to 1993, when he moved to the city with the equivalent of about just fifty dollars.
Wang continues to face court-imposed high-spending restrictions, after his Amer shares were frozen by a Qingdao court due to contractual disputes.
He stepped down as chairman of Shenzhen Amer, a main subsidiary of the group, in October 2023.

name: Krishna Kumar Bangur
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2024); Hurun Global (2018-2022); Hurun India (2017-2019)
forbes_bio: Descendant of the storied Bangur clan of Kolkata, Krishna Kumar Bangur is the chairman of Graphite India, a maker of graphite electrodes.
The company was set up in 1962 in collaboration with Great Lakes Carbon, an American firm.
The company supplies leading steelmakers in India and overseas.
forbes_facts: Bangur joined the business at the age of 16.
Graphite India has featured in Forbes Asia's list of Best Under A Billion companies.
